# Terra computer Runner component

This component runs a human browser scenario in an isolated local Chromium profile. It uses `gpt-6.1-terra` with low reasoning initially, OpenAI's native `computer` tool, and the same 13 selected official Playwright MCP tools used in the 28 October TestOps comparison. The model receives an initial screenshot, then screenshots after native computer actions. It may request MCP observations. The additional read-only `browser_inspect_target` tool resolves a current top-level accessibility reference to a visible point for native computer input. It detects a covered center and samples other visible points without clicking, scrolling or focusing. It reports disabled state while retaining coordinates that hit the visible target. It returns no point for a hidden, fully covered or unsupported frame target. It also reports the current focused element, whether the exact requested control has focus, and its tab index. Runner can use normal native Tab navigation and verify focus before keyboard activation. Inspection never moves focus or dispatches input. Keyboard access does not relax task restrictions. This is a current hit test and focus observation, not a guarantee about the application action or later layout. The prompt gives the scenario, friendly named parameters, initial URL and actual browser host platform (macOS, Linux or Windows); it adds no TestOps-specific action instructions.

The Product execution service selects Luna medium by default. The standalone component default described above stays separate, and explicit private test settings remain available.

The component is separate from the installed agent plugin. Its programmatic `run` and `runScenario` APIs provide an integration seam. A model's final text is a claim; the caller must independently verify saved application data. No memory, JEV or action review is added. Transient provider HTTP responses are retried quietly at the current logical request.

Requests use the provider's automatic prompt-cache defaults. Runner does not set a cache mode or TTL; actual cache usage and charges require provider evidence.

After a successful MCP `browser_resize`, Runner synchronizes the same selected
page's native Playwright viewport. The MCP connection and native owner otherwise
keep separate viewport settings: a later native screenshot can restore the old
size. Screenshots and native input retain the requested size, and switching tabs
retains each page's size. Failed resize replies keep their original error and
uncertainty for the next model turn. If MCP succeeds but native synchronization
fails, that reply also retains the actual native error. Runner does not replay
the browser action.

Native initial, post-action and terminal screenshots capture the current selected
viewport through a Run-owned Chromium CDP session without awaiting font readiness.
The capture session reapplies that page's existing viewport and observed pixel
ratio; it does not select a new size or change application styles. Font loading,
fallback text and blank or unreadable rendering remain visible evidence, not
proof of readiness or a test verdict. Capture errors retain the ordinary incomplete
result and earlier observations. Existing selected-page/navigation checks,
Stop/deadline and retained-image dialog handling apply before and after awaits;
the owned context closes the capture session during cleanup.

## Model instructions

[request-instructions.mjs](src/request-instructions.mjs) owns the initial browser guidance, recap, popup notices, evidence-reference message, report guidance and action limits. [runner.mjs](src/runner.mjs) supplies the observed launch mode, current references and task data. Keep application examples in test fixtures rather than default instructions.

The separate [execution-status.mjs](src/execution-status.mjs) owns the report tool schema and validator; [case-evidence.mjs](src/case-evidence.mjs) owns optional grouped-test guidance. Tool descriptions remain with their tools. Inspect all of these contributions when reviewing an emitted request. Source checks do not establish model quality.

Target inspection keeps complete labels and button/link text, and records the
existing labeled parent chain of the center hit without local clipping. A
`disabled` result describes application state; a returned point is geometric
data, not action permission. Inspection never changes the control or dispatches
input. Native pointer input still has the browser's actual disabled behavior.

## Programmatic use

```js
import { run } from "@katalon-loki/computer-runner";

const result = await run(
  {
    requestId: "caller-stable-identity",
    scenarioId: "T1",
    scenario: "Create a Manual test suite containing a manual test case.",
    params: {
      "Test suite name": "Example suite",
      "TestOps email": email,
      "TestOps password": password,
    },
    target: {
      initialURL: "https://example.katalon.io/project/123/home",
      allowedHosts: ["katalon.io", "katalon.com"],
    },
  },
  {
    apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY,
    artifactDirectory: "/absolute/private/empty-directory",
    signal: abortController.signal,
    onEvent: (event) => {
      /* redacted call/action summary */
    },
  },
);
```

`scenario` is complete human text or a complete structured test record; `params` is required, including `{}` when empty. IDs correlate results and never load scenario content. Parameter names and values are passed separately, without replacing placeholders. `target.initialURL` is required in this version: an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL without embedded username/password. This includes caller-authorized local development targets such as `http://127.0.0.1:5173`. The same URL rule applies to the `runScenario` API. Provider transport still uses HTTPS and browser certificate verification is unchanged. Existing-session attachment and unresolved credential references are not implemented; the host resolves credentials before calling. Hostname restrictions are temporarily disabled for dogfooding at the human’s request. `allowedHosts` remains accepted for saved-request compatibility and does not restrict navigation. The caller may omit `artifactDirectory`; the component creates a private temporary directory. An explicit artifact directory must be empty. The caller owns further retention and deletion. The component requires Node 22.13+. Before its first browser launch, the pinned Playwright installer downloads compatible Chromium into its shared per-user cache. Later runs reuse that version. Installed Google Chrome is not required or modified. Browser downloads use the same execution time bound and AbortSignal; an already-stopped run downloads nothing. Download failure returns an incomplete browser run with zero provider requests; `terminal.actor` and `terminal.reason` retain the cause.

The existing browser navigation observer continues recording requests and browser lifecycle failures. Its hostname predicate temporarily accepts all destinations, including sign-in redirects; caller-provided `allowedHosts` no longer stops a Run. Browser ownership, explicit task instructions and Stop still apply. This temporary change is the human-selected dogfooding behavior, not a new hostname-list requirement.

Initial document navigation uses the Run's remaining time. Stop and the actual
Run deadline interrupt that wait.

An ordinary navigation error does not terminate unrelated requested work. Its
original error stays in the private navigation/MCP records, with uncertain
effects unchanged. The initial navigation also returns its actual error as data
alongside the initial browser observation. It does not assert that the requested
page loaded, retry the action or grant another destination. After owned cleanup,
an available recap receives the original failed-navigation record so earlier
observations cannot silently omit that later failure. Explicit Stop, the Run
deadline and actual navigation-controller failures retain their separate behavior.

Owned loopback Runner fixtures verify zero forbidden destination requests for the original redirected initial/MCP/native-refresh paths, an off-host return chain, 301/302/303/307/308, POST 307/308 bodies, popup/noopener/redirect paths and iframe-triggered top navigation. Known off-host iframes and non-document assets remain permitted. A worker-generated redirect and worker forwarding, including a forwarded redirect, are covered without disabling service workers. These changed-path results do not rewrite the original route-only strict-prevention FAIL evidence. They do not establish universal zero egress, zero DNS/socket activity, non-network or CacheStorage/synthetic-worker containment, special-host behavior, retroactive protection, or containment after a browser/controller failure. The session-detach fixture observed an already-held allowed request resume before cleanup.

The existing route guard and observation latch remain as defense and fail-stop behavior. A violation or guard failure stops later actions/provider dispatch and Runner observation outputs, skips terminal page-content capture and closes owned resources. Fetch remains active until owned browser closure. Before the work decision, policy failure, Stop, worker failure and deadline yield incomplete execution without replay. The checked disposition and cause are frozen before capture/cleanup; later guard, Stop and deadline observations are recorded separately without changing that decision. Earlier trace or official MCP capture may already contain data; checks around capture are not an atomic confidentiality guarantee. The private `navigation-policy.json` records classification counts, the first violation and any route/Fetch callback failure.

Native inputs require a live selected owned page. Tab binding uses the pinned MCP `browser_tabs` Result indices and page identities across explicit sequential new/select/list/close operations in the default owned context. Omit `isolatedContext` or use the explicit `"default"` alias. The exposed schema and caller guidance permit only this context; unsupported named contexts and other values are rejected before upstream dispatch, tab creation or navigation. The argument is never silently removed and no isolation is claimed. Titles and URLs are display data. Unknown page order, unexpected open/close events, malformed metadata and tab-tool failures leave native input unbound; no focus, URL or first-page fallback is used. General concurrent tab creation and multiple-context selection are not supported.

After a verified final-tab close, the selected executor is absent. The pinned MCP's next `browser_tabs list` calls `ensureTab` and creates one blank page. Runner accepts that transition only from a known empty inventory with no selected page, one exact open event, one live owned `about:blank` page and consistent Result selection metadata. It waits at most 500 ms for lifecycle delivery, within the task deadline, without replaying the list. Missing, additional or contradictory events leave native input unbound and retain the original error and uncertain-outcome record for the next model turn. A list is not generally effect-free, and text or URL equality alone cannot bind a page.

A native click, double click or keypress can open one popup. The association remains available during settlement and observation, and at most one following passive wait or screenshot. New popup evidence is eligible for five seconds after the original input; both page-open and window-open events must fall within that window. Evidence already observed in that window can be verified later when a passive wait arrives. The association ends before a new effectful input or an unsupported tool call. Empty `browser_snapshot` and owned-default `browser_tabs list` calls are also safe observations; they retain the original evidence window without renewing it. Ref-based inspection and file-producing observations are outside this recovery path. This is a host limit, not permission inferred from timing: CDP must still report exactly one user-gesture window-open without disowned features, the page must have the exact selected page as its opener, and the complete owned page set must remain stable. Modifier clicks, `noopener`, `noreferrer`, expired associations and multiple page changes stay unbound. Runner confirms the pinned MCP tab order with `browser_tabs list`, then selects that exact popup. It returns a fresh screenshot and marks the remaining requested actions and response calls unexecuted. It does not replay them. If a safe MCP read races with the popup, Runner keeps the original rejected read and its binding diagnostic, verifies the exact popup independently, and makes a separate fresh read. It does not relax MCP tab admission. Recovery captures use unused numeric screen names. A later capture cannot overwrite an earlier image or change its retained hash. The private `popup-binding-<action>.json` receipt records the source action, page identities and skipped action count.

The bounded association supports delayed link handlers without treating every later tab as the result of an earlier click. The [HTML activation model](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#tracking-user-activation) leaves transient activation duration to the browser. The current [Chromium implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromium/chromium/main/third_party/blink/public/common/frame/user_activation_state.h) uses five seconds for ordinary builds. Runner keeps its own fixed limit and the native gesture check; it does not extend browser activation or infer the cause of an unbound popup.

Screenshots and native inputs address page content, not browser chrome. Exactly Meta+R (including existing Command aliases) is an explicit browser command: it refreshes the selected page directly through `page.reload`, without sending a page key event. Page keydown cancellation does not apply to this command. Other keypresses remain literal; CTRL is Control and Meta+A selects all in a focused macOS text field. Refresh waits for `domcontentloaded`, not application hydration or verified persistence.

If refresh opens a `beforeunload` dialog, the requested MCP handler chooses whether to leave. A successful explicit dismissal settles the cancelled refresh on the unchanged document instead of waiting for a new document. The operation records `completion: "cancelled-by-beforeunload"` and a null navigation response. It issues no second reload and leaves the interrupted batch's remaining actions unexecuted. Acceptance keeps the ordinary reload wait. An unconfirmed handler or Stop does not certify cancellation.

MCP initialization and tool listing use the Run's remaining time instead of the
SDK's default 5-second session timeout. The existing 60-second tool-call timeout
stays separate. The Run deadline, Stop and navigation-guard failure interrupt
initialization and the first page binding. Failed setup stops before provider
dispatch or application input; it does not retry the browser task. Cleanup closes
the same owned MCP and browser.

Trusted Node hosts may set `RunOptions.headless` to a boolean. Omission preserves headed Chromium; automated isolated checks explicitly select `true`. This is not a public MCP/model argument. The private protocol records `browserLaunchOptions`, and the same native browser, input path and cleanup remain in use.

Each run creates a fresh private Chromium profile. Its password breach check is
disabled so a browser-owned warning cannot block page input after an approved
application sign-in. This preference applies only to the new run profile. The
creator rejects existing paths and preserves existing browser settings. TLS,
Safe Browsing and the navigation guard keep their existing configuration.
[Chromium defines this preference](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/refs/heads/main/components/password_manager/core/common/password_manager_pref_names.h)
separately from those protections.

A trusted host may also supply the optional `RunOptions.applicationContext` descriptor and async handler. It adds only `application_context_query`, separately from the 13 MCP tools and the provider sender. The handler receives original provider/call identity and already available observation references, and returns the exact original service JSON string. Dispatch retains output order and the original function call ID, checks Stop/deadline after awaits, and writes a separate private `application-context-calls.json` ledger. Retrieval is not a browser/MCP input or a test verdict. Product admission, JSON IPC and setup are documented in the [application-context service guide](../application-context-query/README.md#optional-runner-consumer). Ordinary runs omit the hook.

Malformed context arguments and failed callbacks return the affected call's
safe error without ending the Run or replaying the query. The private ledger
keeps original argument text, dispatch state, returned unusable values and error
details; diagnostic-write failure does not discard an available source response.
No raw host diagnostic is sent to the model. Actual Stop and the original Run
deadline still interrupt the wait.

The matching Product parent/worker/context bridge contains failed or malformed
replies per invocation, retains unresolved error replies and keeps available Run
progress. Compose that receiving group with native dispatch. A completed Run may
still have a host callback outstanding: the private receipt's `pendingHostCalls`
and `hostCallsSettlement` describe promise settlement, not successful source
retrieval or cleanup. They do not authorize another query or action. No prompt,
provider schema, model setting or budget changes in this receiving repair.

A completed pinned `browser_handle_dialog` reply that reports no related modal state has not accepted or dismissed a dialog. With the same known live selected page and unchanged owned page inventory, Runner retains that original tool error, records its no-action basis and returns it to the model so work can continue. It does not retry the dialog command. Other returned tool errors and lost replies also reach the next model turn; their outcome uncertainty stays in the ledger rather than automatically terminating execution. A failed tab operation keeps native input unbound. An unchanged observed Page inventory can support a later explicit selection; a stable count alone is not an identity proof. Runner does not automatically replay the failed call or require a new mandatory investigation phase. Stop, navigation policy and the Run deadline retain precedence. Real Chromium/MCP controls cover continuation, held-dialog accept/dismiss, a lost reply after an actual dismissal, interruption and changed-page refusal. The earlier held-dialog controls add a fixture-only owner listener and open the modal between model turns; those controls alone do not establish the ordinary native-action path.

Bounds default to 80 model calls, 150 returned browser inputs and 10 minutes. `limits` may lower them. An `AbortSignal` stops between browser inputs, aborts a pending provider request and cancels an active official MCP call through the pinned SDK signal option or a Meta+R refresh through the pinned public Playwright signal option. The remaining run deadline also bounds these calls. Stop acknowledgment remains separate from confirmed worker/browser cleanup and does not prove that an in-flight effect was undone. On Stop or an exhausted deadline, terminal UI capture is skipped with an explicit private manifest receipt so a pending document cannot delay owned cleanup. A provider request and its response body use the remaining run deadline, capped at 120 seconds per attempt. Transient HTTP 408/409/429 and 5xx responses, and completed browser replies containing a computer call with no `action` and either absent `actions` or an empty `actions` array, share at most three attempts with 1s then 2s backoff. A missing/empty-action reply has applied no browser inputs; its replacement uses the same last accepted observations, never its rejected response ID. Pending safety checks retain their existing handling. Exhausting this shared allowance preserves the malformed responses and the existing recap/assessment recovery. Retry-After seconds or dates extend those waits up to 30s. Each provider attempt consumes the caller’s existing model-call budget; retries cannot extend that budget. Stop and the remaining run deadline interrupt waits and pending requests. Only the unchanged serialized request is resent; previous_response_id and browser state are preserved. Transport failures with no complete response, invalid successful JSON, invalid input/auth errors and browser execution are not retried. The final summary separates execution state from the unverified test verdict, model termination, API or transport failure, input count, known estimated fee, unknown-usage requests, trace and cleanup. `costPer10kInputs` uses returned browser inputs, excluding waits, screenshots and independent verification. The caller must enforce durable `requestId` reuse before invocation; this component does not persist an idempotency registry.

Browser action and recap requests always send `store: false` under Hai's
whole-Kaijan ZDR direction (#4781). There is no storage opt-in.
The run owns its conversation history through the final recap. Direct OpenAI
uses one WebSocket with incremental response-ID continuation. After a completed
connection closes, the next request replays history, including encrypted
reasoning and original tool-call/output IDs. A missing cached response can also
recover through HTTP. HTTP-only host senders replay the same context through
their selected route. Each physical request/reply is retained privately in
`provider-session-*.json`.

A transport interruption after dispatch leaves inference completion unknown.
Stop aborts the request and closes the socket. Browser actions are dispatched
only from the owner's admitted response. The socket and in-memory history are
released after reporting. Ordinary stateless replay restores the computer tool
schema when earlier computer outputs require it. Tool-free recap materializes
the same history separately. When multiple ordinary images accompany computer
outputs, it quotes the original computer call/output metadata and supplies each
unchanged screenshot as an image part. It keeps image order and repeated frames,
and omits the unused computer definition while action selection remains disabled.
Stored history and normal execution are unchanged; withheld sensitive frames are
not restored. ZDR enrollment requires its own account/project verification.

After cleanup is attempted, a settled continuation can still produce its recap
when cleanup reports an error. The original cleanup result remains recorded;
it does not erase the observations. An explicit Stop still cancels reporting
requests as well as browser execution.
Recap inputs do not assert browser closure. The actual cleanup inventory retains
that outcome separately from the application observations.

## Browser clarification and recovery contract (#2334)

The strict `execution_status` function reports `needs_input`, `stuck`, `blocked` or
`complete`. The action instruction uses `needs_input` only when the task cannot
be completed without an answer from the caller. Missing information by itself
does not require a question. Browser `executionState`
is `completed` for an explicit `complete` report. Unfinished work and uncertain
effects remain in that report; they do not reject completion of execution or
establish a passing application test. Stop, deadline and failures before that
terminal decision yield `incomplete`. The checked disposition is frozen before
capture/cleanup: a later cleanup deadline or Stop cannot contradict accepted
completion. Cleanup observations remain separate in `cleaned` and `cleanup.json`. `terminal.actor` and `terminal.reason` retain the cause.
Final prose or capture alone is insufficient. Completion and step reports are
model-authored and unverified. Independently observe the application outcome;
returned actions do not prove steps. `testVerdict` remains `unverified`.

New browser execution reports use `loki.runner.execution-report/2` without a
`completedSteps` list. The separate chronological recap remains the execution
account used for assessment and display. Status, reason, remaining work, evidence,
questions and effect certainty remain in the control response. Historical v1
reports retain their original completed steps. The existing clarification
transport keeps its array field empty for new reports.

A trusted Node host may supply `options.requestClarification(request, signal)`,
returning `Promise<{answers: Record<string, unknown>, sensitiveQuestionIds?: string[]}>`. It is a host function,
not execute input. The request shape is:

```ts
{
  schema: 'loki.runner.clarification/1',
  clarificationId: string, providerResponseId: string, callId: string,
  reason: string, completedSteps: string[], remainingSteps: string[],
  evidence: string[], questions: {id: string, question: string, kind: string}[],
  provenance: 'model-authored-unverified'
}
```

`clarificationId` is SHA-256 of the response ID, a NUL separator and the call ID.
The current model tool asks for `id`, `question` and `kind`. Receiving uses the
original string ID and nonempty question text, including empty/whitespace IDs. A missing, blank or unusable category
must not discard that question or its answer: native and host known views use
the existing generic `task-scope` category while retaining the complete original
report/request privately. This category supplies no permission or source proof;
answers still bind by the unchanged original ID. Valid categories and valid
neighboring source presentations keep their existing view. Runner no longer sends the
former clarification-source catalog or requires an optional presentation proof
before invoking the caller. Historical valid presentation hints can still
establish a literal source quotation. A missing, changed or unusable hint leaves
the protected original question available as unverified model wording; it does
not invent a quotation. Empty supporting report strings remain valid through
the receiving transport, just as they are in the execution-report decoder.

Question arrays do not need unique or nonblank string IDs. Known views retain
all usable original questions in order, including repeated IDs and different
wording under the same ID. A caller value remains under that exact original key;
Runner does not merge questions, assign replacement IDs or split that value.
A null entry, non-string ID or unavailable question text cannot erase usable
neighbors. Complete raw arrays remain in the private authored report and clarification
record, while the callback receives only usable entries. The caller reply stays unchanged; the saved reader retains
its existing unavailable-artifact gap alongside the usable exchange. A
needs_input report with no usable question returns the correlated
clarification-unavailable error while retaining the report/progress; it does not
wait on an invented question or replay an action.

Supporting report prose and lists are not a reason to lose a usable status or
question. Missing or unusable reason text has the existing empty-string view;
completed steps, remaining work and evidence labels retain their string entries
in order. Missing/non-array lists have an empty known view. The private original
model report remains complete. Evidence retention still selects only actual
names in this Run's saved ledger; normalization does not authorize file access,
create observations or change status/effects. Native callback/snapshot and host
live/saved parsing use the same known forms. The current model declaration and
instructions are unchanged. Required control/question fields and
other predicates remain in the unfinished removal audit.

Historical source selections keep the complete quote and offered choices without
the former 512-character and eight-choice maximums. Parameter source ordinals
are not limited to four digits. The native helper and shared receiving contract
must be updated together; an older consumer can still reject or discard these
selections. Exact source hashes and literal quote membership remain unchanged.
This does not add presentation hints to the current model tool or approve the
remaining cardinality, source-role or template restrictions in the active audit.

The caller's reply goes directly to Runner's AI as the tool result. It is not
filtered, split into matched/unmatched groups or judged complete before delivery.
Text, numbers, booleans, objects, arrays, null and blank values remain as supplied.
A callback that returns no JSON value is represented as null in the JSON wire.
The host's question/Run routing and saved answer receipts remain separate from
interpreting the answer. No extra model turn is added.
Declare newly sensitive full answer values with `sensitiveQuestionIds`. Repeated
or absent-value declarations do not discard the answer; existing marked values
remain protected, including unmatched and structured context. Marked structured
values register their keys and primitive echoes before continuation and public
reads; the saved assessment view masks that whole marked value. Collection and
saved/live accumulation iterate through wide arrays and distinct values rather
than expanding them into a JavaScript argument list. Saved clarification
protection must succeed before recovering individual unusable questions: if its
inputs cannot be read or collected, clarification evidence remains unavailable
instead of projecting neighboring echoes with an incomplete set of secrets.
The remaining Run/report progress and original private files stay intact.
Omission declares no new
sensitivities and does not remove existing protection. Declaration omission,
array order and values stay part of the exact private answer receipt.
Public pending/report/UI text is projected with the maintained per-run redactor.
The customer reader uses opaque question aliases and maps them to the original
private IDs for answering. Known secret values and available exact private
producer identities are masked; this is not a general generated-prose
confidentiality guarantee. Unavailable protection originals cause explicit
withholding, never a raw fallback. Answers may supply steps, preconditions,
fixtures,
expected results or parameters within the original authorization; the request
carries no grants and cannot expand authority. An unavailable or failed callback
returns a correlated error to the same
conversation while preserving the original unanswered report. A private error
record retains the failure and any returned answer; diagnostics are not echoed
to the model. Runner does not repeat the callback or an application action.
Actual Stop and original deadline still interrupt the wait. The original request
remains immutable. If the live callback
receives an answer, the same worker, browser and provider history continue through
the tool-call response; waiting consumes the original deadline.

Unused optional metadata does not invalidate an otherwise usable execution
report, question or legacy source presentation. The original native report
retains it privately. Callback requests, execution snapshots and typed readers
select their existing known fields; they do not forward unknown diagnostics as
public content or new assessment evidence. The current model-facing
execution_status tool declaration stays unchanged. This does not establish the
necessity of remaining kind, required-field, cardinality or source-role checks.

The parent, worker, live manager, customer alias adapter and saved-protection
reader accept the same partial/extended answer. The customer adapter translates
known aliases and keeps unmatched labels separate if they collide with a private
question ID. It never overwrites a matched answer. Saved assessment context does
not require complete question coverage. `answered` records native acceptance of
that response; it does not establish that every question was answered or any
application check passed. Original records, live Run pairing, Stop and the
original deadline remain unchanged. Compose these consumers together: an older
receiver can reject partial context or withhold its saved view.

The saved native question/answer reader retains the same protected unverified
wording when a historical source presentation cannot be verified. Assessment
receives it as separately attributed task context, never as an application
observation or a new grant. Original request, answer and report bytes stay
unchanged. The current adapter and library advertise `bound`, `unverified` and
`unavailable` together. Historical two-state catalogs remain valid baselines;
update the adapter and library together so an older adapter does not withhold the
new question state. This changes no card or form resource identity.

An unexposed MCP function or undecodable/non-object arguments also return a
correlated tool error without dispatch. The private call ledger retains the
original arguments and the undispatched failure. Refusing an unusable command
does not erase an existing selected-page binding or terminate the Run. The
provider can use its existing tools and observations; no compulsory correction,
fresh observation or application replay is added.

The ordered dispatcher shares that decoding/error path before classifying a
pending native-popup observation. A malformed command immediately after native
input therefore returns its own error; it does not close the pending transition,
replace the selected page or erase earlier actions. Usable commands retain their
existing popup handling. The original bad arguments remain in the private call
ledger, and the same conversation may continue with its requested work. No
additional observation, retry or action is forced.

`blocked`, `stuck` and uncertain effects are model-authored reports, not runtime
stop commands. Runner saves the original report and acknowledges it so the same
conversation can continue. This removes the former status-based stops under the
human direction on [#4449](https://github.com/katalon-studio/loki/issues/4449) and
[#4529](https://github.com/katalon-studio/loki/issues/4529). It adds no required
investigation, observation or confidence gate. Actual Stop, deadline, browser
command decoding and access enforcement remain separate.

When assessment recap is enabled, reporting is separate from browser execution.
After verified browser cleanup, one tool-free Luna medium request summarizes the
same retained conversation. Its single attempt has a 120-second provider timeout
and a 4,096-token output allowance, outside execution's call and time limits.
Stop still cancels it; refusal or failure does not start a replacement request.
The usage ledger includes this extra request in the task total.

Recap receiving has no step-count or serialized-byte cap. Structured JSON may
span output text parts or messages. Independently complete JSON documents retain
their string steps in the original order; an unreadable document or invalid row
does not discard usable steps elsewhere. The original reply remains in
`recap-response.json`. This handling adds no model request or browser action.
Provider completion, Stop and action-producing reply handling remain separate.

An explicit completion retains its report binding, including when action
effects remain uncertain. Ending actions does not suppress reporting. New terminal
records bind the exact response and status-call IDs, rather than comparing reason
text. A valid blocked v2 report may have no selected evidence IDs; that does
not remove the observations retained in its conversation. An execution limit can instead use the last fully settled continuation,
including the exact pending tool outputs, when no later activity is missing from
that continuation. Duplicate tool call IDs are refused before any call in that
response executes, so one output cannot stand for an unfinished batch. Response
and call IDs must be nonempty strings. A recorded enforcement
failure suppresses limit-ended recap; the navigation guard’s own deadline alone
does not. The Run remains incomplete, and the recap identifies the
unfinished work. A navigation violation, failed cleanup or Stop do not authorize
a recap on the existing limit-ended path. No browser action or historical task is replayed.
Assessment keeps the recap attributed to that Run and does not infer that
remaining checks were performed.

A provider failure before any action in its reply executes also retains a recap.
This includes malformed action replies, missing or duplicate proposal IDs, and
responses truncated by the browser turn's output allowance. Incomplete responses
retain their output-limit reason before proposal validation. No proposal in a
rejected reply executes. The recap uses the exact input to that failed turn and
its last accepted response, or the initial observations when the first turn
fails. It does not continue the rejected reply or fabricate tool outputs for it.
After cleanup, the same tool-free request and original Planner assessment can
report the available evidence. The browser Run and its original failure remain
incomplete; no browser action is replayed.

A completed provider reply containing final prose but no action or status report
also keeps its available observations for the requested recap. Execution remains
incomplete and the original final prose and any earlier obstacle report stay
recorded. Recap continues the accepted final response with no invented tool
acknowledgement; when that response has no usable ID, it uses the actual preceding
request input. Stop still cancels reporting. A missing completion report does not
prove application success and does not require another execution request.

With normal recovery, the first `stuck` raises effort from low to medium once
within the original limits. Later `stuck` reports, reports at a higher effort and
uncertain effects no longer end execution. Missing input does not consume this
escalation. Acknowledging a report does not replay an application action.
Stop, deadline and exhausted limits still end execution. `effortAccounting` counts provider
attempts, including retries, by the requested effort. Desktop Runner does not
support this clarification or recovery contract.

The first provider request sends all saved-record path IDs in
`savedEvidenceReferences`. Continuations send only new or changed paths.
Earlier references stay in the provider response chain. A repeated path refreshes
that reference. Hashes and byte counts stay in the private host ledger, outside
this model view. Browser observations, images, scenario history and saved
artifacts remain in full.

The strict `execution_status` schema has a stable string-array evidence field.
Runner preserves every supplied label as unverified model data. A missing or
unadvertised label does not discard the report. Only records in this Run's
host-owned saved ledger have evidence references and original-byte checkpoints;
model labels never open a filesystem path. Transient HTTP retries keep the same
request bytes and reference snapshot. Completion may have an empty evidence
list. Record availability does not prove an application result.

A missing or unusable `effects` label does not reject a usable status report or
its questions. The full supplied value remains in the private original report.
Known progress views include a recognized supplied label only; absence does not
mean known effects, uncertain effects or successful application behavior.

An invalid `execution_status` returns its actual decoding/validation error in
the matching tool response. The next turn keeps the normal tool set and has no
forced status tool choice, report-only phase or single-correction quota.
Malformed reports and their errors remain in
`invalid-execution-status-*.json`; they are not rewritten as valid reports.
The model can use an available browser tool or submit another report within the
same existing call/time limits. The host does not replay any prior application
action. Multiple reports, case boundaries and usable application commands in one
response are handled in their original order, with a matching output for each
call. Completion is decided after that response's commands settle; actual
unfinished native input remains unfinished. The recap receives the complete
settled continuation, including earlier reports and command outputs. Separate
malformed reports in one response keep separate numbered original records in
the private manifest. Clarification and remaining action/consumer restrictions
stay under the complete #4529 audit; this increment does not establish those
paths.

This reduces repeated host metadata and keeps the tool schema stable. It does
not set a cache policy or guarantee a cache hit, token count or fee reduction.

## Browser provisioning

No browser is bundled in the package. `prepareBrowser` from `@katalon-loki/computer-runner/browser` uses the packaged Node and the pinned Playwright installer, with `chromium --no-shell`. It installs full Chromium for both headed and new-headless consumers, without a second headless-shell distribution. Playwright owns its cache, install locking and incomplete-download recovery. The standalone API honors Playwright cache/download settings from its trusted host environment; the plugin worker uses the ordinary cache for its host user. Browser preparation is lazy: importing the API, plugin discovery and source analysis do not call it.

The owned Chromium CDP port-file wait uses the remaining original Run time and actual Stop signal. A port file that becomes visible after five seconds no longer ends an otherwise usable Run. The existing port decoding and selected owned-browser attachment remain unchanged. Real Chromium controls delay only that file visibility, then check continuation, actual Stop and original deadline with owned cleanup.

The private `browser-install.log` and protocol retain provisioning evidence. The scenario prompt, native computer actions, selected MCP observations and independent-verification boundary remain in use; the recovery contract above permits one Terra reasoning escalation.

## Standalone CLI

The standalone adapter and historical usage notes are retained in
[experiment 2173](../../experiments/_shared/capability-cli/README.md). The notes
include former paths; the relocated adapter is under `experiments/_shared/capability-cli`.
Product calls the Node API directly; its package contains no CLI bin.

## Private evidence and Playwright trace

Marked values and their JSON-escaped forms use literal, leftmost-longest matching in one pass. Existing redaction markers remain atomic and newly inserted markers are not reinterpreted as values. Large caller values therefore do not fail because a generated regular expression exceeds the JavaScript engine's pattern size. Authentication-query and private-image handling remain unchanged.

Each native screenshot also retains a separate `screen-initial.ui.json` or
`screen-N.ui.json` text observation. It records the screenshot hash, separate
capture times and latest native action index. The screenshot and text are not an
atomic capture. The record contains a read-only accessibility snapshot of the
selected page body, with known secrets removed. It adds no browser input and is
not sent to the Runner model, including in the evidence-reference list. Reads
have a 1.5-second limit and stop with the run. Failed reads retain an unavailable
record without inventing page content. Reports can select each JSON record
through the existing manifest and secret-protection checks. A later secret
answer also applies when the record is read. Raw screenshots remain private
when the run has marked secrets. This does not capture states between native
screenshots or prove content in an inaccessible frame.

The output directory must be owned by the current user and inaccessible to group and others. It contains full private `request-N.json` and `response-N.json` records, `transport-N.json` with HTTP status and selected response headers, plus distinct `request-N-attempt-A.json`, `response-N-attempt-A.json` and `transport-N-attempt-A.json` records for every attempt (including retry status and actual delay), browser action records, screenshots, browser storage state, terminal UI evidence, `manifest.json` with hashes, and `playwright-trace.zip`. The trace starts before initial navigation and stops in the cleanup path even when the model API fails. It captures Playwright calls, browser screenshots, DOM snapshots and browser network activity. It can contain credentials. Do not commit, share or copy it to a report folder. Open it locally with Playwright Trace Viewer.

The model API call is Node `fetch`, outside Chrome. Its HTTP 500 cannot appear in the Playwright browser trace. `transport-N.json` records its HTTP status, request ID if provided, elapsed time and selected rate-limit headers. A failed request without a usage object has an **unknown charge**, not zero cost. The component does not claim a provider billing receipt. Every attempted HTTP request contributes to attemptedRequests and requestsWithoutUsage; any returned usage, including an error response, contributes to the known estimate. The private calls list contains one row per attempt. Recovered errors produce no public terminal event.

The [control-flow diagram](../../experiments/_shared/agent-execution/docs/runner-flow.md) describes the existing research Runner. This component's specific path is shown in [flow.md](flow.md).

`terminal-ui.original.json` retains the private unmodified terminal observation;
`terminal-ui.json` is its protected projection for the existing consumer path.
When the end-of-execution capture succeeds, the existing recap request receives
the selected page's final screenshot. It can compare the final state with
earlier action screenshots. When known sensitive input or redacted page content
requires private pixels, the recap receives only the protected accessibility
snapshot as context. The capture adds no browser input or model request.
Private original responses, clarification records and checkpoints stay unchanged.

Each complete top-level computer action has a fixed 250 ms settlement before the
next action. Compound click, modifier and drag events stay atomic. An empty
computer call keeps one settlement; a nonempty call has no extra batch wait.
Stop, deadline and navigation-guard failure interrupt settlement; selected-page
and navigation guards apply before further dispatch. Completed input receipts
remain completed when a later wait stops the batch. The original provider list
and action rows distinguish the dispatched prefix from the undispatched suffix.
One screenshot is returned at the end of the call. This finite timing mitigation
does not establish target readiness; a menu delayed beyond it can still be missed.

Native input errors retain their original action receipts and return with the
correlated computer observation. The unexecuted suffix of that action list is
reported, without replaying the failed input or dispatching that suffix. A later
model turn can continue independent requested work. Actual Stop, caller limits
and navigation access errors still interrupt execution. A returned error does
not establish whether a partially dispatched action took effect or change a
saved verdict.

Browser host settings accept `model: "gpt-6-luna"` with `reasoning` set to `none`,
`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`. Terra still accepts `low` and `medium`,
and Terra low remains the default. Set `effortRecovery: false` for a fixed effort
comparison. A stuck report continues at that selected effort. With normal
recovery, only low can move to medium once. Receipts retain the requested model,
effort, recovery choice and selected model Standard cost estimate. The estimate
is not a provider billing receipt. No model access check occurs before dispatch.

### Case evidence in browser Runs

When `planRef` supplies an exact Plan answer ID, result digest and selected test
IDs, Runner exposes a `test_case` recording tool. It declares the current case
before input and ends it after the final observation. Boundary calls can share
a response with browser input and retain their original order. They do not authorize execution or retries and do
not prove coverage or a verdict. Repeated visits keep separate occurrence IDs.

The original whole-Run trace contains named case groups. `case-evidence.json`
records computer action IDs and groups existing manifest-bound screenshots by
case. It adds no screenshots and omits typed text. Inputs outside declared boundaries stay in
`unassignedActions`; the full trace retains setup and MCP activity. A stopped or
unfinished case stays interrupted. Old Runs are never rewritten or re-executed to
add this index. Evidence recording does not change the native test verdict.

### Native JavaScript dialog lifetime

After the initial page/MCP setup and first viewport capture, Runner keeps JavaScript dialogs open for the exposed MCP handler instead of allowing its owner connection to dismiss them. A native action that opens a dialog remains `awaiting-dialog` until its original promise settles, including release of its held modifiers. A keyup dialog yields to the same handler; the key release and original input are not repeated. The remaining actions in that computer call are not run or automatically replayed. Other browser inputs and case changes return an unexecuted result while that input is pending; a complete execution report cannot conceal that unfinished native input. A dialog opened independently between model turns, with no pending native input, does not require another browser action before completion; ordinary owned cleanup closes it.

Page pixels cannot be captured while the modal blocks Chromium. The computer reply reuses only the last actual capture of the same bound page, explicitly identifies it as retained rather than fresh, and supplies the observed dialog text as application data. It writes no invented screenshot or DOM evidence. The existing MCP handler keeps the accept/dismiss/prompt choice; no automatic acceptance is added. Runner observes ordered dialog-open/closed events through the existing owned Page session. An observed closure can settle the original native promise even when the handler reply is lost. The tool error and unknown-outcome record remain unchanged; observed closure is not a confirmed handler reply. A still-open modal remains pending, and a second modal gets a separate handoff. No new browser connection is opened while the modal blocks Chromium. A closed or changed page binding cannot dispatch the handler against another page.

Stop and the existing Run deadline wake native input waits. Cleanup skips blocked page capture, retains unfinished action state and closes only the owned context. Real Chromium/pinned-MCP controls cover native click/keyboard activation, modifier-release dialogs and successive choices, confirm accept/dismiss, prompt/alert, sequential choices, case attribution, unexecuted input, interruption, lost replies and closed-page refusal. They use controlled provider replies, not a paid model or native Codex session. Initial-navigation dialogs before the first viewport/MCP binding remain outside this repair's qualification. The first auto-dismissed native confirmation and failed listener-only prototype remain on [#4715](https://github.com/katalon-studio/loki/issues/4715); the original banking result is not replayed or accepted by these controls.
